conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. You've been brought in tonight because you're having chest pain and there's concern about an infection in your neck. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I’ve had this sore spot on my neck for a few days. It’s getting red and tender. And earlier tonight, I had a tightness in my chest again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any fever, chills, or shortness of breath with the chest pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No fever, but my neck feels warm. The chest pain wasn’t bad this time—just pressure, no sweating or trouble breathing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Given your history of heart disease and past stents, we always take chest pain seriously. We’ll monitor you and check your heart enzymes. But your EKG just now looked stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had this before. It comes and goes. But the neck thing is new. Is it infected?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it looks like cellulitis—skin infection. We’ll start antibiotics. We’re not seeing signs of an abscess yet, so no procedure needed for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t want to stay long. I’ve got things to do. Can’t I just get a shot or a prescription?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand, but with your medical history—heart disease, prior heart attack, hepatitis C—we need to make sure you’re stable. The antibiotics work best if given through an IV at first.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been through worse. I’m not staying overnight. Last time I was here, they kept me for a rash and chest pain, but it was nothing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see your record from three years ago. But this is different. You have an active infection now, and we can’t risk it spreading, especially near your neck.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I get that, but I feel okay. Can I just take pills and leave?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’d prefer to observe you for a few hours to make sure the antibiotics start working and your chest symptoms don’t worsen. It’s for your safety.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate it, doc, but I’m leaving. I’ll take my chances.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I strongly advise against that. If you leave against medical advice, the infection could spread, or you could have a heart event without help nearby.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know the risks. I’m still leaving. Can you at least give me something to take with me?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I can prescribe oral antibiotics, and I’ll give you a prescription for pain if needed. But please follow up with your doctor in 24 hours. And if chest pain returns, come back immediately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright, I’ll try. Thanks for explaining.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re documenting that you’re leaving against medical advice. A nurse will go over discharge instructions and give you the prescriptions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll be careful.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Please call your cardiologist about the chest pain. And avoid any strain until you’re seen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I don’t need another hospital stay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re here to help. Take care, and please don’t hesitate to come back if things change.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Appreciate it, doc.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will be in shortly to finalize your discharge paperwork.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready when they are.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care, and stay safe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks again.
